comments.author: NiLSPACE
comments.story: Mozilla and Microsoft are rebuilding their browsers’ foundations
comments.why: Talk explaining how WebRender sends pages to the GPU.
comments.text: If you have the time there is a nice talk about WebRender: [VIDEO] Here is another great talk: [LINK] At ~25:30 he'll also talk a bit about Quantum. In a nutshell WebRender is used to send a web page to the GPU which will paint all divs, borders, shadows, images etc. Currently WebRender is the only component I'm aware of that is inside Firefox Nightly. It's still behind a config though.

comments.author: littlestymaar
comments.why: Example of state of the art GPU rendering tools in Mozilla's new pipeline.
comments.text: You should take these advices with a grain of salt because it refers to the legacy rendering pipeline used by current web browers. There is not absolute rule stating that layout and painting must be slow while compositing is not. In fact Mozillians are currently working on a new rendering pipeline[1] based on state of the art rendering tools[2]. This new pipeline should be deployed in firefox in 2018 as a part of the ongoing Quantum project. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
